# DISSEMINATED MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM DISEASE TREATMENT

Many of these patients have HIV/AIDS. Management is complex. Consult Infectious Diseases.
Rifabutin is optional for disseminated disease. Rifabutin can improve cure rates, but may decrease blood concentrations of many drugs. Consult Infectious Diseases or Pharmacy for more information.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued for 12 months and until CD4 count is >100 cells per microliter for at least 6 months.

References:

- Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Opportunistic Infections in HIV
- Infected Adults and Adolescents. AIDSinfo (2015) 1-282
- Mandell chapter: Mycobacterium avium complex
- Sanford keyword: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare
- Up-to-Date article: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections in HIV-infected patients
Therapy:
## Two-drug treatment

Preferred treatment

Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h ($$) [R]
Alternative
Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h ($) [M] <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h [R]

## Three-drug treatment

Preferred treatment
Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h($) [R,DI] <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h ($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO q24h ($$) [R,DI]
Alternative
Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h ($) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h [R]
<AND> rifabutin 300 mg q24h ($$) [R,DI]
